properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is a declared transitive dependency (yarn.lock) shipping SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/SHA-512/RIPEMD-160 stream implementations. Part of the shipped dependency tree of web3-provider-engine; no first-party call site found in this repo — consumed transitively by EthereumJS-era packages. Hashes are Grover-only, low PQ urgency; recorded as dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: createRandomId uses Math.random() to mint JSON-RPC payload ids; consumed by util/create-payload.js for request correlation. Non-cryptographic PRNG in first-party code — real, but these are correlation ids, not security tokens (impact limited to request-id guessability/collision). Hygienic fix: crypto.randomInt(). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is Ethereum's transaction/message-signature curve, fixed by the Ethereum protocol — replaceable only by the protocol itself, not by this library; what IS changeable here is the library version. @noble/curves is a runtime transitive dep (via @ethereumjs/util, @ethereumjs/tx, @metamask/eth-sig-util) and is actively exercised by this engine's own first-party signing call sites at subproviders/hooked-wallet-ethtx.js:36,49,58,69 (tx signing, eth_sign, personal_sign, EIP-712).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signatures available in the shipped @noble/curves API surface (same package as the secp256k1 the engine actually uses). No first-party Ed25519 call site in this engine — it exists in the dependency inventory because the library ships it; reachable by any consumer of the engine's dependency tree. Quantum-unsafe (Shor); deadline risk class, not harvest risk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is resolved transitively in the dev chain (browserify-sign depends on it; ganache test chain also pulls it) — see also the LIB-a0bfbc1a package entry. This engine's own ECDSA signing path goes through @noble/curves instead (subproviders/hooked-wallet-ethtx.js); no first-party elliptic call site found, but the library ships in the resolved tree and is wired into the browserify-sign bundle path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 declared transitively via @noble/curves@1.3.0 in yarn.lock; noble's P-256 ECDSA/ECDH ships in the dependency tree, reachable via ethereum-cryptography/@metamask packages. No first-party P-256 call site in this repo (Ethereum signing here is secp256k1). Recorded as shipped-library inventory; replaceable only via dependency updates.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH/ECDSA machinery declared transitively via elliptic@6.5.4 (yarn.lock); ships quantum-vulnerable elliptic-curve key agreement and signatures in the dependency tree. No first-party ECDH call site found. Note: 6.5.4 predates the 6.6.x signature-malleability hardening, so the shipped version is also behind on classical fixes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key agreement available via tweetnacl 0.14.5, resolved transitively in the dev/browser chain (tweetnacl@1.0.3 also resolved at yarn.lock:5127). No first-party X25519 call site in this engine. If any consumer uses it for key agreement it is harvest-now-decrypt-later class; the capability ships in the tree regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak-256 (required from ethereum-cryptography at test/subproviders/etherscan.js:1) used in a test to compute the 4-byte Ethereum ABI selector of "getLatestBlock()" while building mocked Etherscan API responses. Real hash operation, in test code. Keccak-256 is symmetric — Grover square-root only, no Shor exposure. Recorded as in-use crypto in the test suite.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The browser-compatible pbkdf2 package (browserify crypto shim chain, resolved at yarn.lock:4320) — the package entry LIB-ea49d4c1 is the same underlying asset viewed as a package. Not Shor-broken (KDF, Grover-limited only); security depends on iteration counts chosen by callers (keystore/BIP39 flows), none of which are in this engine's first-party code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 declared transitively via @noble/hashes@1.3.3 in yarn.lock; ships SHA-2 family hashing in the build's dependency tree (reachable via ethereum-cryptography/@metamask packages). No first-party call site found. Dependency-inventory line; Grover-only exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 available in the shipped @noble/hashes API surface (runtime hash library behind @ethereumjs/util / @metamask/eth-sig-util). No first-party BLAKE3 call site; @ethereumjs/util uses keccak256/sha256 from the same package. Hash, Grover-limited only; post-quantum-adequate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt declared transitively via scrypt-js@3.0.1 (yarn.lock); memory-hard password KDF ships in the dependency tree. No first-party call site found. Symmetric KDF — not Shor-vulnerable; cost parameters are decided by whichever consumer invokes it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/keccak from @noble/hashes is the runtime hash provider for the Ethereum stack this engine drives: keccak256 runs inside @ethereumjs/util / @metamask/eth-sig-util for tx hashing, EIP-191 personal-message hashing and EIP-712 typed-data hashing — reachable from this engine's own call sites (subproviders/hooked-wallet-ethtx.js:48). Quantum-relevance is Grover-limited (hash), not Shorn-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5's authenticated encryption (secretbox/stream) available in the resolved tree — same tweetnacl package as the X25519 entry. No first-party call site in this engine. AE scheme, Grover-limited only; post-quantum-adequate for its purpose.

properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 declared in yarn.lock — ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, Ed25519 signatures and X25519 key agreement (all Shor-vulnerable) in the dependency tree. 0.14.5 is a 2017-era release; @metamask/eth-sig-util elsewhere in the lockfile pulls the newer tweetnacl 1.0.3, so two versions ship. No first-party call site found — presence is the inventory question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 declared in yarn.lock — SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256 streaming implementations shipped in the dependency tree. No first-party call site found. Dependency-inventory line.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is the pure-JS EC crypto library resolved at yarn.lock:2764 (transitive: browserify-sign depends on it for its ECDSA path, and the ganache dev chain pulls it). Ships secp256k1/P-256 ECDSA + ECDH; quantum-unsafe (Shor) — see the ALG-710f61f0 ECDSA algorithm entry for the same package's primitive. No first-party call site; it is wired into the browserify bundle path used by the yarn bundle scripts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.3.3 is the runtime hash library behind @ethereumjs/util and @metamask/eth-sig-util — the code paths this engine invokes for keccak256 (tx hashing, EIP-191, EIP-712), plus sha256, ripemd160, BLAKE3 and SHA-3 in its API surface. The engine's hashing all happens inside this library; the algorithm-level entries for it are ALG-979eccf8 (BLAKE3) and ALG-c9ef78a4 (SHA-3), same package, and keccak is the one this engine actually exercises.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 resolved at yarn.lock:3405 — SHA-256/SHA-512/RIPEMD160 hash implementations, pulled transitively by elliptic (its hashing dependency). No first-party call site; ships in the resolved dev/browser tree. Hashes are Grover-limited, not Shor-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context

Consumed transitively (ethereum-cryptography, @metamask packages); the P-256 algorithm it provides is recorded separately as ALG-a6da3577. No direct first-party call site.
